note: Writing and speaking tasks and 0–5 area marks prepare learners for B1 Preliminary and B2 First formats using original tasks and plain B1–B2 descriptors (not endorsed by or affiliated with Cambridge).

writingDescriptors.intro: Writing is marked 0–5 on four areas, with no overall score. Each area gets one short strength and one short improvement in plain B1 English. Teachers can change any mark.

criteria.label: Content
criteria.question: Did you answer every part of the task?
criteria.band5: All parts answered clearly with relevant detail. Fits the reader.
criteria.band3: Most parts answered; one part is thin or missing.

criteria.label: Communicative achievement
criteria.question: Does it sound right for your reader?
criteria.band5: Right tone and format (email, article, story). Holds the reader's interest.
criteria.band3: Mostly the right tone; format works.
criteria.band1: Wrong tone or format; hard to read as that text type.

criteria.label: Organisation
criteria.question: Is it easy to follow?
criteria.band3: Grouped ideas and simple linkers, with a few jumps.
criteria.band1: Little order; few or misused linkers.

criteria.label: Language
criteria.question: Are your grammar and words clear?
criteria.band5: Good B1+ range; tries the week's grammar; errors don't confuse.
criteria.band3: Everyday words and simple grammar; some errors, meaning clear.
criteria.band1: Frequent basic errors sometimes hide the meaning.

rules: Length. Target word counts stay 120–150 words for Weeks 1–4. Under 100 words caps Content at 3. Over 180 words adds the tip "Try to keep to 120–150 words."
Week goals. Required points, linkers, and the week's grammar become checks feeding Content, Organisation, and Language rather than separate marks.
Corrections. At most 3 corrections per text, putting the week's grammar first, and keeping clear, correct sentences as they are.

Spelling and honesty. British spelling is taught; American spelling is noted once but not marked as an error. Pasted text is flagged where a teacher is involved, and teachers can change any area mark.
writingDescriptors.learnerFeedback: Four area marks (0–5) with no overall score; one-sentence strength and one-sentence improvement per area in B1 English; at most 3 corrections (the week's grammar first); and an improved B1–B2 version that keeps clear sentences as they are.

speakingDescriptors.intro: Speaking uses four areas (0–5 where marked), with one-sentence strengths and improvements in plain B1 English. Pronunciation is marked by a teacher only, and Interactive communication is marked by AI in Discuss and decide only.

criteria.label: Grammar and vocabulary
criteria.question: Did you use clear grammar and the right words?
criteria.band5: Good everyday vocabulary; tries the week's grammar; errors don't block meaning.
criteria.band3: Simple grammar and vocabulary; errors are noticeable, main point is clear.
criteria.band1: Very limited words or frequent errors make the message hard to follow.

criteria.label: Discourse management
criteria.question: Did you speak for long enough and link your ideas?
criteria.band5: Full answer for the task length, relevant, connected with simple linkers.
criteria.band3: Answers the prompt but briefly, or repeats a couple of linkers.
criteria.band1: Very short turns or unconnected fragments.

criteria.label: Pronunciation
criteria.question: Could people understand you easily?
criteria.band5: Easy to understand throughout; clear stress and endings.
criteria.band3: Mostly clear, with occasional effort needed on stress or sounds.

criteria.label: Interactive communication
criteria.question: Did you answer your partner and keep the talk going?
criteria.markedBy: AI in Discuss and decide only
criteria.band5: Responds to the partner's point, asks back or invites their view, helps reach a choice.
criteria.band3: Answers what's asked and takes turns, rarely builds on the partner's idea.
criteria.band1: One-word replies or talks past the partner.

notes: Pronunciation is never marked by the AI. Learners still get "Practise these sounds" from words in their transcript, and teachers can add or change any mark.
Cue-card points are shown as a checklist (✓ / ✗), not a mark. Only the long turn is required to finish the week; Questions about you, Discuss and decide, and Follow-up questions are optional.
learnerFeedback: 1. Marks (0–5) on Grammar and vocabulary and Discourse management (plus Interactive communication in Discuss and decide), with one strength and one improvement each.
2. Cue points covered as a ✓ / ✗ checklist on the long turn.
3. "Your answer, improved" keeping the learner's ideas with 2–4 tappable target-structure highlights and a cached British TTS play button (or "Another example" first if under ~20 words or off-topic).
4. "Practise these sounds" and "Take with you" highlights checked on retries.
speakingDescriptors.recordings: Four model answers, British English, natural pace (about 130-150 words a minute), with transcripts; 12 shadowing clips at normal and 0.8 speed with transcripts.

placement.intro: Placement takes about 35 minutes at sign-up and sends each learner to the foundation course, Stage 1 or Stage 2. The EF SET starting test is taken alongside it as the progress baseline, but placement makes the decision.

parts.what: 24 questions: 10 grammar, 6 vocabulary, 4 reading (one short text), 4 listening (two short clips)
'Tell me about your job or studies, and what you'd like to be doing in two years' time.' 60 seconds, 30 seconds to plan.
'Write 80–100 words about a recent trip or event: what happened and what you enjoyed most.'

questionBlueprint.focus: Past simple, comparatives, can / have to, everyday vocabulary
Present perfect vs past simple, future forms, first conditional, modals, B1 vocabulary
Past perfect, passive, second conditional, relative clauses, collocations
Reported speech, third conditional, modals of deduction, B2 vocabulary

bands.description: 'Getting there' on most criteria: short, simple sentences; frequent errors that sometimes block meaning.
'On target' on most criteria: the task is done clearly; errors do not block meaning.
'Beyond target' on most criteria: some range and longer, linked sentences.
'Beyond target' on all criteria: wide range, accurate complex sentences, well organised.

decisionRules.samples: Or both samples at A2, whatever the test score.
At least one sample at B1 or above.
Both samples at B1+ or above.

placement.borderline: If the score is within one point of a boundary, or the test and samples point to different results, place the learner in the lower option and tell them they can take a short move-up check after week 2. Where a teacher is involved, they review borderline cases first.
placement.learnerChoice: A learner placed in Stage 2 may choose to start at Stage 1. A learner placed in the foundation course is shown why, with links to suitable A2 material.
placement.efSetCrossCheck: If the EF SET result differs from the placement by a full CEFR level or more, the placement is flagged for review; it is not changed automatically.

checkpoint1.intro: A course checkpoint, not a CEFR placement or certification test. It assesses B1 grammar, a short spoken narrative and a 150-word piece, and is reported beside the learner's EF SET starting test.

quiz.blueprint: Four Main items and one Light item per week, written separately from the practice item bank so the checkpoint tests learning, not memory of practice items. Order: weeks 1–4, Main then Light. Exclude stretch tasks.
quiz.delivery: Each item is auto-marked; the reason is shown only after the whole checkpoint is submitted. Short scenarios and answer keys allow valid variants; if two options are grammatical, ask which better expresses the stated meaning or accept both.
quiz.reporting: Report results by skill and recommend a specific practice item.

items.prompt: We ___ the Colosseum when we were in Rome in 2019.
My brother ___ three different jobs since he left university.
items.reason: 'Since he left' connects the past to now.

items.prompt: The sun ___ (shine) when we left the hotel.
When I opened the fridge, I realised someone ___ (eat) my cake.
items.reason: It happened before I opened the fridge.

items.prompt: As a teenager, I ___ have very long hair.
items.reason: 'Have' (possession) is a state, so would is not possible.

items.prompt: A: Any plans for the summer? B: I ___ visit my cousins in Ireland, but I haven't booked anything yet.
items.reason: An intention with nothing arranged yet.

items.prompt: We ___ (fly) to Lisbon on Friday. The tickets are in my bag.
I'll send you the photos when I ___ home.
items.reason: After 'when', use the present simple for the future.

items.prompt: As soon as the film ___ (finish), we'll go for dinner.
items.reason: After 'as soon as', use the present simple for the future.

items.prompt: If I ___ the lottery, I'd buy a house by the sea.
In the UK, you ___ drive on the left.
If you want to improve your English, you ___ read a little every day.
My grandmother ___ (can / not / use) a smartphone, so we phone her.
___ I leave my bag here while I go to the toilet?
Put the words in order: Where / you / do / work?
Cheese ___ (make) from milk.
items.reason: A general fact; the cheese is the focus.

items.prompt: Most of the city's buses ___ by electricity now.
The first email ___ (send) in 1971.
Our flight ___ because of the snow.
This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
items.reason: 'Where' for a place followed by a full clause.

reserves.prompt: I ___ (not / see) her since the wedding.
Don't worry, I ___ (call) you before I ___ (leave).
reserves.reason: Will for the promise; present simple after before.

reserves.prompt: You ___ (not / have to) come to the party if you're tired.
The Alhambra ___ (visit) by millions of people every year.

checkpoint1.reserveUse: Reserves replace an item that pilot data shows is unclear, or form a retake for learners repeating the checkpoint.

prompts.label: A. A change I got used to
prompts.text: Describe how life was before a change, what happened, what was difficult, and how things are now.

prompts.label: B. A note for a visitor
prompts.text: A friend is visiting your town for a weekend. Recommend what to see: include a regular event or custom, one fact about a place's past, a comparison, and one piece of advice.

conditions.value: In the app; pasting disabled; no phrase bank or model
AI bands on the four writing criteria straight away; a teacher confirms where one is involved, and the teacher's mark counts

writing.onTarget: 'On target' or better on at least three criteria, task achievement not 'Getting there'. Results guide practice; they never block week 5.

result.intro: Results are reported by part and by week, never as pass or fail. Learners continue to week 5 whatever their result; the checkpoint guides practice, it does not block progress.

thresholds.onTarget: 'On target' or better on at least three criteria, and task achievement not at 'Getting there'
'On target' or better on at least three criteria, and task achievement not at 'Getting there'

result.practiceLinks: Each part below target links to the matching practice: weak quiz items to that week's extra items and grammar clinic, speaking to the week's shadowing and conversation, writing to a revise-and-retry task on the same prompt.

calibration: A second teacher checks every checkpoint item for a single correct answer and accepted variants.
Check the existing 24 placement questions against the blueprint (6 A2, 8 B1, 6 B1+, 4 B2) and replace those that do not fit.
Mark 10–20 sample texts and recordings by hand and compare with the AI's bands; adjust prompts until they agree on at least 8 in 10.
After 30 placed learners, compare placement with EF SET results and adjust the cut scores (11/12 and 18/19).
Review any checkpoint item that more than 90% or fewer than 30% of pilot learners answer correctly.
Confirm the checkpoint thresholds (70% quiz, three of four criteria) against teacher judgement of pilot learners.

speaking.intro: After week 4, learners record one short spoken narrative under checkpoint conditions, marked with the same four descriptors.
speaking.prompt: Talk about a time when you had to adapt to something new: a job, a place, a course or a routine. What was it like before, what happened, and how are things now? If you like, say what you would tell someone in the same situation.

conditions.value: 1 minute; notes allowed, no phrase bank or model
One recording; no retry (practice tasks allow retries, checkpoints do not)
AI bands on the four criteria straight away; a teacher confirms where one is involved, and the teacher's mark counts
"On target" or better on at least three of the four criteria, with no criterion at "Getting there" for task achievement
Weeks 1-4: narrative tenses, present perfect, used to / would, modals for advice; featured vocabulary from any of the four weeks

speaking.transferNote: The prompt is new, so it tests transfer rather than memory of a practised answer.
